source.title: Do Models Share Safety Representations? Cross-Model Steering for Safe Visual Generation
source.authors: Tobia Poppi; Silvia Cappelletti; Sara Sarto; Florian Schiffers; Garin Kessler; M. Cornia; L. Baraldi; Rita Cucchiara

record.tranche_reason: The study uses activation-space safety directions as a tool for cross-model steering of image and video generators. Its results concern unsafe visual generation, not refusal behavior in safety-trained chat models.
record.gate_note: The study derives safe-versus-unsafe directions in source LLMs, transfers them to generative-model text encoders, and reports their effects on unsafe visual-generation rates. Those results do not measure refusal to a user by a chat model, so they do not test any listed claim version. The study's reported steering outcomes are recorded as findings about a related, different construct.
record.test_reason: The study builds a safe-minus-unsafe content direction from mean-pooled final-layer LLM states. It maps that direction into the text encoders of image and video generators and reports its own method's unsafe-generation ASR and quality. It never measures refusal by a chat model toward a user, and it never ablates or adds a refusal direction in an LLM. Arditi et al. is cited only as motivation, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also claim that transferred directions often match or surpass the native target-side oracle while preserving CLIP similarity. They read this as evidence that safety structure is shared across models and modalities. Their own tables show sizeable FID costs for SVD, which tempers the claim that quality is preserved.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates mean safe-minus-unsafe displacements from paired prompts in a source LLM, maps them using benign anchors, and adds the calibrated vector to a target image or video model's text-conditioning representations. It does not use the original chat-refusal ablation or measure refusal.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported safety–utility outcome varies with alignment mapping and steering strength; the text also reports different trade-offs across target backbones.

fits_no_version.finding: A safe-minus-unsafe content direction from Llama3.1-8B, Mistral-7B or Qwen3.5-9B, mapped through benign anchors, lowers I2P ASR in all four image generators. SVD gives the largest drops, e.g. Flux1-Schnell 0.307 to 0.038 (Llama, SVD).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A diff-in-means safety content direction from an LLM transfers to image-generator text encoders and reduces unsafe generation without target-side unsafe data.

fits_no_version.finding: For Wan2.2 video with Llama/SVD, ASR falls from ∼0.75 at α = −3 to ∼0.07 at α = 5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The transferred safety direction also reduces unsafe text-to-video generation as steering strength increases.

fits_no_version.finding: SVD transfer costs quality: on Z-Image FID rises to 73.5 (Llama, SVD) versus 31.7 for the original model. Ridge and MLP mappings give smaller ASR reductions with better FID and CLIP-Sim.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transferred safety steering has a safety-quality trade-off that depends on the mapping and on α.

record.problems: The evaluation is limited to the source and target models, categories, languages, and benchmarks considered. The authors note that strong steering can reduce prompt fidelity, visual quality, or legitimate benign content. Results are largely reported as point values without uncertainty estimates; some qualitative and trade-off findings are presented in figures.
record.rows_left_out: The study reports more results than extracted here. Omitted Table 1 comparator results include string-based steering; omitted Table 2 results include non-SVD transferred mappings and native, random, and string-based comparators. Also omitted are the remaining CLIP-Sim/FID table entries, steering-strength sweeps, multi-category steering, magnitude-calibration ablations, source-scale comparisons, and entity-removal experiments (Secs. 4.2–4.3 and Appendices C.1–C.5, Figs. 3, 5–9). These concern visual-generation safety and utility rather than the listed chat-refusal claim versions.

untested.parts: All parts: chat-model refusal, ablation removing refusal, addition inducing refusal, and capability preservation in LLMs.
All parts: weight-edit abliteration of released chat models.
All parts: jailbreak suppression of the direction and adversarial training against its ablation.
All parts. Appendix C.4 only speculates that larger LLMs encode safety 'more distributed', and that concerns content directions, not refusal.
All parts: separating the harm judgment from the refusal decision.
All parts. The transfer here is of a content-safety vector from LLMs to diffusion text encoders, not a refusal direction across languages, variants or base/instruct models.
All parts: the effect of refusal training on the direction.

record.verdict_notes: All rows report the study's own method and its baselines on visual-generation safety. None measures LLM refusal. The record's T4/uses_without_test is defensible; cites_only/T6 would also be reasonable, since the refusal direction itself is never used. The native, random and string-based comparators are baselines for the study's method, not evidence on the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Chat-model refusal, all-layer/all-position ablation, harmless-request refusal under addition, and preservation of chat abilities.
Weight-edit removal of refusal in released chat models.
Jailbreak suppression of a refusal direction and training against its ablation.
Whether chat refusal is affine, conical, or distributed across multiple directions.
Separation of harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision in chat models.

Transfer of the claimed chat-refusal direction across languages, chat-model variants, or base and instruct chat models; this study instead transfers a safety steering vector to image/video generators.
How refusal training affects whether a removable direction exists.

rows.note: Target-side text encoder is T5-XXL. The study describes α = 5 as the setting for models other than Z-Image-Turbo.
